field.definition: A set with addition and multiplication operations satisfying field axioms

ring.definition: A set with two binary operations generalizing addition and multiplication

group.definition: A set with a single binary operation satisfying closure, associativity, identity, and inverse

ideal.definition: A subset of a ring closed under ring addition and multiplication by ring elements

module.definition: A generalization of vector spaces where scalars come from a ring

vector space.definition: A set of vectors with scalar multiplication and vector addition operations

basis.definition: A linearly independent spanning set for a vector space

dimension.definition: The cardinality of a basis for a vector space

homomorphism.definition: A structure-preserving map between algebraic structures

isomorphism.definition: A bijective homomorphism with homomorphic inverse

kernel.definition: The preimage of the identity under a homomorphism

image.definition: The set of all output values of a function

quotient.definition: The result of dividing one algebraic structure by a normal substructure

coset.definition: A translate of a subgroup within a group

abelian.definition: A group or structure in which the operation is commutative

generator.definition: An element from which all others can be derived by the group operation

automorphism.definition: An isomorphism from a structure to itself

endomorphism.definition: A homomorphism from a structure to itself

tensor product.definition: A construction combining two modules into a single module

direct sum.definition: A coproduct in the category of modules or abelian groups

exact sequence.definition: A sequence of maps where the image of each equals the kernel of the next

commutative.definition: Satisfying a*b = b*a for all elements

distributive.definition: Satisfying a*(b+c) = a*b + a*c for all elements

identity element.definition: An element e such that e*a = a*e = a for all a

inverse.definition: An element a^{-1} such that a*a^{-1} = e

subgroup.definition: A subset of a group that is itself a group under the same operation

subring.definition: A subset of a ring closed under ring operations

subfield.definition: A subset of a field that is itself a field

extension field.definition: A field containing a given field as a subfield

Galois group.definition: The group of automorphisms of a field extension fixing the base field

polynomial.definition: A finite sum of terms each being a product of a coefficient and variable powers

root.definition: A value at which a polynomial evaluates to zero

eigenvalue.definition: A scalar lambda such that Av = lambda*v for some nonzero vector v

eigenvector.definition: A nonzero vector v such that Av = lambda*v for some scalar lambda

determinant.definition: A scalar value encoding linear independence properties of a matrix

trace.definition: The sum of diagonal entries of a square matrix

matrix.definition: A rectangular array of numbers representing a linear map

linear map.definition: A map preserving addition and scalar multiplication

span.definition: The set of all linear combinations of a given set of vectors

linearly independent.definition: A set of vectors with no nontrivial linear combination equaling zero

orthogonal.definition: Having inner product equal to zero

symmetric.definition: A matrix or form equal to its transpose

antisymmetric.definition: A matrix or form equal to the negative of its transpose

bilinear form.definition: A map linear in each of two arguments separately

manifold.definition: A topological space locally homeomorphic to Euclidean space

fiber.definition: The preimage of a point under a bundle projection

bundle.definition: A space locally a product of a base and fiber

open set.definition: A set belonging to a specified topology

closed set.definition: A set whose complement is open

compact.definition: Every open cover has a finite subcover

connected.definition: Cannot be partitioned into two disjoint nonempty open sets

path.definition: A continuous map from [0,1] to a topological space

homotopy.definition: A continuous deformation of one map into another

homeomorphism.definition: A bicontinuous bijection between topological spaces

continuous.definition: Preimage of every open set is open

convergence.definition: A sequence or net approaching a limit

limit.definition: The value approached by a sequence or function

neighborhood.definition: An open set containing a given point

metric.definition: A function defining distance between points in a space

norm.definition: A function assigning a nonnegative length to each vector

Hausdorff.definition: A topological space where distinct points have disjoint neighborhoods

covering.definition: A collection of sets whose union contains a given set

fundamental group.definition: The group of homotopy classes of loops based at a point

homology.definition: A sequence of abelian groups measuring holes in a topological space

cohomology.definition: The dual theory to homology using cochains

simplex.definition: The convex hull of affinely independent points

CW complex.definition: A topological space built by attaching cells of increasing dimension

orientation.definition: A consistent choice of handedness for a manifold

boundary.definition: Points in neither the interior nor the exterior of a set

interior.definition: The largest open set contained within a given set

closure.definition: The smallest closed set containing a given set

dense.definition: A set whose closure is the entire space

nowhere dense.definition: A set whose closure has empty interior

Baire category.definition: Classification of sets as first or second category in a topological space

paracompact.definition: Every open cover has a locally finite open refinement

regular.definition: A topological space separating points from closed sets by open sets

normal.definition: A topological space separating disjoint closed sets by open sets

Urysohn.definition: Related to Urysohn's lemma on separation by continuous functions

Tietze.definition: Related to the Tietze extension theorem for continuous functions

quotient topology.definition: The finest topology making a quotient map continuous

product topology.definition: The coarsest topology making all projections continuous

derivative.definition: The instantaneous rate of change of a function

integral.definition: The accumulation of quantities over a domain

series.definition: The sum of terms of a sequence

sequence.definition: An ordered list of mathematical objects

divergence.definition: A sequence or series that does not converge

uniform convergence.definition: Convergence where the rate is uniform across the domain

pointwise convergence.definition: Convergence at each individual point of the domain

Cauchy sequence.definition: A sequence where terms become arbitrarily close to each other

complete.definition: A metric space in which every Cauchy sequence converges

inner product.definition: A generalization of the dot product to abstract vector spaces

dual space.definition: The space of all bounded linear functionals on a normed space

functional.definition: A map from a function space to scalars

spectrum.definition: The set of scalars lambda for which an operator minus lambda is not invertible

resolvent.definition: The inverse of operator minus lambda for lambda in the resolvent set

Fourier series.definition: Representation of a periodic function as a sum of sinusoids

Fourier transform.definition: A transform decomposing a function into frequency components

Laplace transform.definition: An integral transform converting functions of time to complex frequency

measure.definition: A function assigning nonnegative extended real numbers to sets

Lebesgue integral.definition: An integral defined using measure theory, more general than Riemann

sigma-algebra.definition: A collection of sets closed under complement and countable union

probability measure.definition: A measure with total mass equal to one

almost everywhere.definition: Except possibly on a set of measure zero

support.definition: The closure of the set where a function is nonzero

convolution.definition: An operation combining two functions by integration over their product

distribution.definition: A generalized function defined by its action on test functions

tempered distribution.definition: A distribution with at most polynomial growth at infinity

Sobolev space.definition: A function space with weak derivatives in Lp

weak derivative.definition: A generalized derivative defined via integration by parts

Green's function.definition: The kernel of the inverse of a differential operator

analytic.definition: Locally representable by a convergent power series

holomorphic.definition: Complex differentiable in a neighborhood of every point

residue.definition: The coefficient of 1/z in the Laurent series at an isolated singularity

pole.definition: An isolated singularity where the function grows without bound

essential singularity.definition: An isolated singularity that is neither removable nor a pole

branch cut.definition: A curve in the complex plane where a multi-valued function is discontinuous

category.definition: A collection of objects and morphisms satisfying composition and identity axioms

natural transformation.definition: A morphism between functors respecting the categorical structure

adjunction.definition: A pair of functors with a natural bijection between morphism sets

colimit.definition: A universal construction dual to the limit

product.definition: A limit of a discrete diagram

coproduct.definition: A colimit of a discrete diagram

pullback.definition: The limit of a cospan diagram

pushout.definition: The colimit of a span diagram

morphism.definition: An arrow between objects in a category

composition.definition: The operation combining composable morphisms into a single morphism

identity morphism.definition: A morphism acting as identity for composition

subobject.definition: An equivalence class of monomorphisms into an object

quotient object.definition: An equivalence class of epimorphisms out of an object

abelian category.definition: A category with zero object, kernels, cokernels, and exact sequences

topos.definition: A category with finite limits and a power object for each object

presheaf.definition: A contravariant functor from a category to sets

site.definition: A category equipped with a Grothendieck topology

Grothendieck.definition: Relating to Alexander Grothendieck's contributions to algebraic geometry

monad.definition: A monoid in the category of endofunctors

comonad.definition: A comonoid in the category of endofunctors

Kan extension.definition: The best approximation to extending a functor along another functor

comma category.definition: A category of triples (object, morphism, object) for two functors

slice category.definition: The comma category for a functor and identity functor

preorder.definition: A reflexive and transitive binary relation

poset.definition: A set with a partial order relation

lattice.definition: A poset where every pair has a meet and join

profunctor.definition: A functor from the product of two categories to sets

enriched category.definition: A category where hom-sets are objects of a monoidal category

2-category.definition: A category enriched over the category of small categories

prime.definition: A natural number greater than 1 with no positive divisors other than 1 and itself

composite.definition: A positive integer with at least one positive divisor other than 1 and itself

divisor.definition: An integer that divides another integer without remainder

gcd.definition: The largest positive integer dividing two given integers

lcm.definition: The smallest positive integer divisible by two given integers

modular arithmetic.definition: Arithmetic where numbers wrap around upon reaching a modulus

congruence.definition: Two integers having the same remainder when divided by a modulus

quadratic residue.definition: An integer that is a square modulo a prime

Legendre symbol.definition: A symbol encoding whether an integer is a quadratic residue mod a prime

Dirichlet series.definition: A series of the form sum a_n / n^s

Euler product.definition: A product over primes representing a Dirichlet series

L-function.definition: A Dirichlet series with Euler product and functional equation

elliptic curve.definition: A smooth projective curve of genus one with a marked point

algebraic number.definition: A number that is a root of a nonzero polynomial with rational coefficients

transcendental.definition: A number that is not a root of any nonzero polynomial with rational coefficients

Gaussian integer.definition: A complex number with integer real and imaginary parts

ideal class group.definition: The group of fractional ideals modulo principal ideals

discriminant.definition: An invariant of a polynomial or number field measuring ramification

conductor.definition: The smallest modulus for which a character is defined

affine.definition: Relating to geometry preserving parallelism but not distances

projective.definition: Relating to geometry of lines through the origin in higher-dimensional space

Euclidean.definition: Relating to classical geometry with distance and angles

hyperbolic.definition: Relating to non-Euclidean geometry with negative curvature

curvature.definition: A measure of how much a curve or surface deviates from being flat

geodesic.definition: A locally length-minimizing curve on a Riemannian manifold

Riemannian metric.definition: A smoothly varying inner product on tangent spaces of a manifold

tangent space.definition: The vector space of tangent vectors at a point on a manifold

cotangent.definition: The dual of the tangent bundle

differential form.definition: A section of an exterior power of the cotangent bundle

connection.definition: A way to differentiate sections of a vector bundle

parallel transport.definition: Moving vectors along a curve while keeping them parallel

Ricci curvature.definition: The trace of the Riemann curvature tensor

sectional curvature.definition: The curvature of a manifold restricted to a two-dimensional tangent subspace

Einstein manifold.definition: A Riemannian manifold where Ricci curvature is proportional to the metric

fiber bundle.definition: A space that locally looks like a product of base and fiber spaces

vector bundle.definition: A fiber bundle where each fiber is a vector space

characteristic class.definition: A cohomology class measuring the twisting of a bundle

spectral sequence.definition: A sequence of pages computing homology via successive approximation

derived category.definition: The localization of the category of chain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms

étale morphism.definition: A flat, unramified morphism of schemes that is locally an isomorphism
